title: Energy, Work and Power Module 6 Lesson 2: Collision Energy Loss Coalescence custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moving at $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal surface collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$. The two particles coalesce. Calculate the loss of kinetic energy caused by the collision.

Particle $P$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ moving right at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides head-on and coalesces with particle $Q$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$ moving left at $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the kinetic energy lost in the impact.

Particle $A$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. It slides $2.5\text{ m}$ down to the bottom where it collides and coalesces with stationary particle $B$ of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$. Find the speed of the combined particle immediately after the collision. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
A particle $A$ of mass $m$ moving with speed $u$ collides directly and coalesces with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $3m$. Calculate the percentage of kinetic energy lost in the collision.

Two coalesced particles of combined mass $5\text{ kg}$ move with an initial speed of $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.4$. Find the distance moved before coming to rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A particle of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moving at $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides and coalesces with a stationary particle of mass $m\text{ kg}$. The collision causes a loss of $18\text{ J}$ of kinetic energy. Find the value of $m$.

questions.prompt: A particle $B$ of mass $6\text{ kg}$ is at rest on a smooth horizontal table. A particle $A$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$ moves on the table with a speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and collides directly with $B$. In the collision, the two particles coalesce to form a single combined particle $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the combined particle $C$ after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the system, the kinetic energy after the collision, and the loss of kinetic energy caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$ is moving along a smooth horizontal track with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It catches up and collides directly with particle $Q$ of mass $2.5\text{ kg}$ which is moving in the same direction along the same line with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The two particles coalesce upon impact.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the common speed of the combined particle after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the system due to the collision.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a smooth slope inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. It slides a distance of $3.6\text{ m}$ down the slope and then smoothly transitions onto a rough horizontal surface with no loss of speed. Particle $P$ travels $2\text{ m}$ along the rough surface before colliding directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. Upon collision, $P$ and $Q$ coalesce and move together with an initial speed of $1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of $P$ at the bottom of the incline, and find the speed of $P$ immediately before the collision with $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By applying the work-energy principle to $P$'s motion across the $2\text{ m}$ horizontal section, calculate the work done against friction and determine the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between $P$ and the horizontal surface.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $1.2\text{ kg}$ is projected down a rough plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.28$ and $\cos\theta = 0.96$. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the plane is $\mu = 0.5$. Particle $A$ moves $2.5\text{ m}$ down the plane from an initial speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to strike a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ on the plane. Upon impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done against friction on $A$ over the $2.5\text{ m}$, the speed of $A$ immediately before impact, and the common speed of the combined particle immediately after coalescence.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy lost during the collision, and find the further distance the combined particle slides down the plane before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: A wooden block $B$ of mass $1.95\text{ kg}$ is suspended from a fixed point by a light inextensible cord of length $1.8\text{ m}$. A projectile $A$ of mass $0.05\text{ kg}$ is fired horizontally at the block with speed $120\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and becomes embedded in the block. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the common speed of the block and projectile immediately after impact, and calculate the kinetic energy lost during the embedding process.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical height $h$ to which the pendulum rises above its lowest position, and find the angle $\theta$ that the cord makes with the vertical at the highest point of the swing.

questions.prompt: Particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $1.5\text{ kg}$ and $3\text{ kg}$ respectively, lie on an inclined plane making an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal where $\tan\alpha = 0.75$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$). The section of the plane from $X$ to $Y$ of length $L$ is smooth, and the section from $Y$ to $Z$ of length $4\text{ m}$ is rough with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.75$. Particle $A$ is released from rest at $X$, slides down to $Y$, and collides directly with particle $B$ which is in limiting equilibrium at $Y$. Upon impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce and continue down the rough section $YZ$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the combined particle arrives at $Z$ with a speed of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the length $L$ of the smooth section $XY$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy lost during the coalescence at $Y$, the total work done against friction over the entire journey from $X$ to $Z$, and the total mechanical energy dissipated from the moment $A$ is released until the combined particle reaches $Z$.

questions.prompt: Three identical particles $A$, $B$, and $C$, each of mass $1\text{ kg}$, lie along a straight line on a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.2$. Initially $B$ and $C$ are at rest with $B$ located $1.5\text{ m}$ from $A$, and $C$ located $1\text{ m}$ beyond $B$. Particle $A$ is projected towards $B$ with an initial speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Particle $A$ strikes $B$ and coalesces with it to form combined particle $AB$. The combined particle $AB$ continues across the floor, strikes $C$, and coalesces with $C$ to form combined particle $ABC$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of $A$ immediately before it collides with $B$, the common speed of $AB$ immediately after the first collision, and the kinetic energy lost in the first collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of $AB$ immediately before striking $C$, the common speed of $ABC$ immediately after the second collision, the kinetic energy lost in the second collision, and the total energy dissipated over the entire sequence until $ABC$ comes to rest.
